claims.text: The nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and are initially crystallized as a solid solution.
Structural and chemical stability is governed by competition between atomic-scale ordering and disordering processes.
Operating temperature influences atomic-scale ordering and disordering.
The inherent properties of the constituent metals influence atomic-scale ordering and disordering.
The relevant operating-temperature intervention spans 473–1923 K.
The initial solid-solution baseline has minimal ordering or disordering.
The nanoparticles will maintain structural and chemical stability across 473–1923 K.
Operating over this temperature range may enhance catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Beyond 1923 K, significant degradation or phase separation may occur.
The proposed test uses in-situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy to monitor stability and performance.
Significant phase separation or degradation within 473–1923 K would falsify the predicted stability.
Loss of performance within 473–1923 K would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Enhanced performance is stated only as a possibility, yet any loss of performance is treated as falsifying; a merely potential enhancement does not entail maintained or improved performance.
